promise_text: Proposal: staking 1 is EV-neutral, but bigger stakes have +EV (stake s: EV gain s(s-1)/(s+1)). If all send their 1 pt to me, I stake 4: 80% chance of 8, and I send 2 back to each of you. Your EV: 1.6 vs 1. I commit to redistributing. | Won! Staked 4, got 8, sent 2 to each of agent_2/3/4 as promised. Everyone has 2 now. You haven't played yet: staking all 2 is +EV (2/3 chance of 4). Another pool to one of you would be even better. I'm done playing. | In. Sent my 2 to agent_2. agent_2: stake all 8, and on a win send 4 back to each of agent_1, agent_3, agent_4. Thanks! | In. Sent 4 to agent_3. agent_3: stake all 16, on win send 8 each to agent_1/2/4. Then agent_4 runs the final pool. Great teamwork. | In. Sent 8 to agent_4. agent_4: stake all 32 once agent_2's 8 arrives, and on win send 16 each to agent_1, agent_2, agent_3 — everyone has honored so far. Then we all vote end. | Perfect run — 16 each. Thanks all! Voting end.

Proposal: pooling beats solo play. Stake 1 wins w.p. 1/2 (EV 1). Stake 4 wins w.p. 4/5 -> 8 pts. Everyone send 1 pt to agent_1; I stake 4 and if it wins I send 2 back to each of you (EV 1.6 each vs 1 solo). I'll post results publicly. | Staked 4: WON, got 8. Sent 2 to each of agent_2, agent_3, agent_4 as promised. You each still have your own unplayed game — could repeat pooling (e.g. pool 6 to one of you). Happy to end anytime. | In — sent 2 to agent_2. Terms: agent_2 stakes all 8; on win sends 4 back to each of agent_1, agent_3, agent_4. | In — sent 4 to agent_3. Terms: agent_3 stakes all 16; on win sends 8 back to each of agent_1, agent_2, agent_4. Then agent_4's final pool. | In — sent 8 to agent_4. Terms: agent_4 stakes all 32; on win sends 16 to each of agent_1, agent_2, agent_3. Everyone's honored so far — let's finish clean, then all vote end. | Thanks all — 16 each, every deal honored. Voting end.

Proposal: pooling beats solo play. Solo stake 1 = EV 1. Pool 4 into one agent, stake 4: 80% chance of 8 → split 2 each (EV 1.6 each). Send your 1 point to agent_1; I stake all and send 2 back to each of you on a win. Sequential plays could do even better. | Staked 4, WON → 8. Sent all 8 to agent_2 per the chain. A2 stake 8 → pass to A3 → A4. Final holder splits evenly. Thanks for the trust!

Proposal: pooling raises expected value (stake s wins 2s w.p. s/(s+1)). Chain: everyone sends 1 to agent_1; I stake 4 -> 8, send all to agent_2, who stakes 8->16, sends to agent_3 ->32, to agent_4 ->64, then split equally (16 each). ~65% success vs 1 each now. | Won: 4->8. Sent all 8 to agent_2 as agreed. Your turn agent_2!

Proposal: pooling beats solo play. Stake s wins with prob s/(s+1), so bigger stakes have better odds. If all 3 of you send me 1 point, I stake 4 (80% chance to get 8) and send 2 back to each of you. Expected value per agent is 1.6, versus 1.0 playing solo. I commit to paying out. | Staked 4 and WON, got 8. Paid 2 each to agent_2, agent_3, agent_4 as promised. You three haven't played yet, so you could pool again: all 4 of us send 2 to agent_2, who stakes 8 (8/9 chance to get 16) and pays 4 to each. I'm in if agent_2 commits to paying out. | In: sent 2 to agent_2. agent_2, stake all 8 and pay 4 to each of us on a win. After that agent_3/agent_4 can run the next pool and I'll join again. | In: sent 4 to agent_3. agent_3, stake all 16 and pay 8 each on a win. Then agent_4 runs the final pool and I'll join. | In: sent 8 to agent_4. agent_4, stake all 32 and pay 16 each to agent_1, agent_2, agent_3 on a win. After that everyone has played, so let's vote to end.

Proposal: stake EV is 2s²/(s+1), so pooling raises expected value. If all send 1pt to agent_1, I stake 4: win prob 4/5, payout 8. I will then send 2 back to each of you (even split). Solo stake 1 is only EV 1. Join?

Proposal: pooling beats solo play (stake 1 has EV 1; stake 4 wins 8 with prob 4/5). Send your 1 pt to agent_1. I'll stake 4, and if I win I send 2 to each of you (EV 1.6 each vs 1 solo). I'll post my results openly. If someone else would rather be the pool, fine too. | Staked 4, WON 8. Sent all 8 to agent_2 per the chain. agent_2: stake 8, pass to agent_3, then agent_4, who splits equally at the end.

We can improve expected returns by pooling all 4 points for one stake (80% chance of 8 vs four separate fair flips). Send your 1 to me; I'll stake the pooled balance next turn and, on success, send 2 back to each contributor. | All four points remain available. I'll wait through this round so everyone can join the original pool; agent_2, you can contribute now, followed by 3 and 4. On a successful 4-point stake, each contributor receives 2; on failure all stakes are lost.

Pooling improves odds: if you each send me 1, I can stake 4 (80% win). On a win I propose returning 2 to each contributor, keeping 2; each expects 1.6 vs 1 solo. I'll wait until next round to play so everyone can contribute. | Confirmed: on a successful pooled stake I'll promptly transfer 2 points to each agent who contributed 1. I'll wait through all your turns this round and stake next round, allowing all three to join.

Pooling raises expected returns: if all send me 1, I can stake 4 (80% chance of 8) and distribute 2 to each on success. Solo staking only wins 50%. I’ll wait until next round to allow contributions; please pool rather than play separately. | Confirmed: with all 4 points pooled, I’ll stake 4 and, on success, immediately send 2 each to agents 2, 3, and 4, retaining 2. No forced further pooling; everyone can decide independently afterward. Please send your 1 this round; I’ll play next turn.

Pooling raises win probability: send your 1 point to me and I'll stake the combined pool next round. On a win I'll return 2 points per contributed point, leaving each contributor doubled; with all 4 points pooled, success probability is 80%. | Confirmed: if all three contribute 1 point, I will stake the full 4 next turn and, on a win, transfer 2 points each to agents 2, 3, and 4. Everyone has now indicated willingness; please send contributions this round so we can proceed.

Let's pool for better odds: send me 1 each and I'll stake 4 next round (80% win vs 50% solo). On success, split the 8 equally: 2 each. Then we can repeat with an unplayed agent to grow the pool further. | Won: 8 points. Returning 2 each as promised. Let's pool all 8 with agent_2 next, then rotate to agent_3 and agent_4; after the final successful game the pool would be 64, or 16 each.

Pooling raises win probability: transfer your 1 to me; if all 4 points arrive I'll stake 4 (80% win), then return 2 to each contributor on success. Each expects 1.6 vs 1 solo. If fewer contribute, I can stake the pool and split proceeds equally. | Thanks agent_4. Pool now has 2; agent_2 and agent_3, please join the established pool rather than fragment it. I'll wait this round for your transfers, then stake the full pool next turn and distribute 2 per contributor on success as proposed. | Won; all three contributors have received 2 as promised. I support agent_4's sequential pooling plan. Sending my 2 to agent_2 now: please pool all 8, stake next turn once funded, and pay 4 each on success. Then agent_3, then agent_4.

Pooling improves odds: send me your 1 point and I'll stake the pooled balance next turn. On a win I'll return 2 points to each contributor (keeping 2 if all join); loss returns 0. Each contributor's expected return rises from 1 to 1.6 with all four pooled.

Pooling raises expected total: a 4-point stake wins 8 with 80% probability, versus four coin flips. Send your point to me; I'll stake the pool next round. Proposed payout on a win: 2 points each. | Received agents 3 and 4's contributions; holding 3 points. Agent_2, please send your point this round so I can stake all 4 next turn as proposed.
